question: What is the main cause of coronary artery disease?

options.A: Infection of the inner heart lining
options.B: Enlargement of the right heart chambers
options.C: Plaque buildup in the coronary arteries
options.D: Weakening of the heart muscle walls

explanation: Coronary artery disease happens when fatty plaque accumulates inside the arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does reduced blood flow in the coronary arteries cause chest pain?

options.A: The heart muscle becomes starved of oxygen
options.B: The lungs fail to expand fully during inhalation
options.C: Fluid fills the space around the heart sac
options.D: Blood pressure rises rapidly in the major veins

explanation: When blood flow drops, the heart muscle does not get enough oxygen. This shortage causes ischemia, which results in chest pain. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which type of cell primarily engulfs cholesterol in the blood vessel wall to form plaque?
explanation: White blood cells called monocytes enter the artery wall and turn into macrophages, which swallow fats to form the foam cells seen in early plaque. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h2)

question: What makes an atherosclerotic plaque particularly dangerous for causing a heart attack?

options.A: A high concentration of healthy red blood cells inside
options.B: An absence of any smooth muscle cells around the core
options.C: A thick calcified shell blocking all blood flow permanently
options.D: A thin fibrous cap prone to sudden rupture

explanation: Plaques with thin outer coverings can easily break open. This rupture triggers sudden blood clot formation that can block the vessel entirely. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following cannot be changed or modified in a patient with coronary artery disease?
explanation: Genetics and family history are fixed factors that cannot be altered through lifestyle adjustments or medications. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: A 52-year-old market trader presents with high blood pressure and high cholesterol. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Administer intravenous antibiotics for potential infection
options.B: Provide education on blood pressure and lipid control
options.C: Prepare the patient for immediate open heart surgery
options.D: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent fluid overload

explanation: Managing risk factors like high blood pressure and cholesterol relies heavily on patient education and lifestyle changes to slow down disease progression. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: How is stable angina different from unstable angina?

options.A: Stable angina causes permanent damage to heart muscle
options.B: Unstable angina responds immediately to nitroglycerin
options.C: Unstable angina only occurs during heavy physical exercise
options.D: Stable angina is predictable and relieved by rest

explanation: Stable angina happens with activity and goes away with rest. Unstable angina is unpredictable and can happen even while resting. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do some patients having a heart attack feel pain spreading to their left arm or jaw?

options.A: Inflammation directly damages the peripheral nerves of the limbs
options.B: Shared spinal sensory nerve pathways converge in the brain
options.C: Blood clots travel directly from the heart into the arm arteries
options.D: Lack of oxygen forces the arm muscles to cramp simultaneously

explanation: Referred pain occurs because the nerves carrying signals from the heart enter the same level of the spinal cord as the nerves from the arm and neck. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which blood test is most specific for detecting damage to the heart muscle during a heart attack?
explanation: Cardiac troponin is a specialized protein that leaks into the bloodstream specifically when heart muscle cells suffer injury. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a coronary angiography in a patient with suspected heart disease?

options.A: To check the total volume of blood pumped per minute
options.B: To measure the electrical conduction velocity across the atria
options.C: To identify active bacterial infections within the heart valves
options.D: To visualize exact blockages inside the coronary blood vessels

explanation: Coronary angiography uses a special dye and X-rays to create an image of the heart blood vessels and locate any blockages. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main way beta-blockers help patients with coronary artery disease?

options.A: Dilating peripheral veins to increase blood return
options.B: Decreasing heart rate and myocardial oxygen demand
options.C: Lowering blood glucose levels in diabetic patients
options.D: Dissolving existing blood clots inside the coronary artery

explanation: Beta-blockers slow down the heart rate and reduce how hard the heart has to work, which lowers its need for oxygen. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why are statin medications commonly prescribed for patients with coronary artery disease?

options.A: To block pain signals traveling from the heart to the brain
options.B: To prevent sudden bronchospasm in patients with asthma
options.C: To lower cholesterol and stabilize the fibrous cap of plaques
options.D: To maintain normal kidney perfusion during fluid shifts

explanation: Statins lower LDL cholesterol and help reduce inflammation, which strengthens plaque so it is less likely to rupture. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h6)

question: What small device is placed inside a blocked heart vessel during a procedure to keep it open?
explanation: A stent is a tiny wire mesh tube that is expanded inside a narrowed coronary artery to keep the blood flowing freely. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main difference between PCI and CABG procedures?

options.A: CABG creates a surgical bypass around blockages using harvested vessels
options.B: CABG is performed through a wrist catheter without general anesthesia
options.C: PCI uses synthetic blood vessels to replace the entire coronary tree
options.D: PCI requires opening the chest cavity to remove damaged heart muscle

explanation: CABG involves open surgery to route blood around blocked arteries using grafts, while PCI uses a catheter threaded through blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h7)

question: A patient reports sudden, tight chest pain. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for laboratory blood results before taking action
options.B: Administer supplemental oxygen and assess pain characteristics
options.C: Discharge the patient home with oral analgesics
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward to relieve stress

explanation: When a patient has active chest pain, the priority is to check the details of the pain and provide oxygen to reduce strain on the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why must a nurse listen carefully to a patient's lung sounds after a heart attack?

options.A: To confirm that the endotracheal tube remains in the correct bronchus
options.B: To evaluate how well the patient is tolerating deep breathing exercises
options.C: To measure the exact electrical resistance of the chest wall
options.D: To detect early signs of pulmonary congestion from heart failure

explanation: If the left side of the heart is weak, fluid can back up into the lungs, creating crackles that signal fluid buildup. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a cardiac rehabilitation program?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for any cardiac medications
options.B: To optimize physical recovery and prevent future cardiac events
options.C: To reverse previous damage to the heart muscle cells
options.D: To surgically remove all existing plaque from every artery

explanation: Cardiac rehab guides patients to regain strength, learn healthy habits, and lower their chances of having another heart problem. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why is psychological support an important part of cardiac rehabilitation?

options.A: Depression and anxiety are common following a major cardiac event
options.B: Counseling replaces the need for physical exercise training
options.C: Patients require formal psychiatric clearance before returning to work
options.D: Mental stress directly dissolves cholesterol plaques in the blood

explanation: Suffering a major heart event often causes emotional distress, which can affect a patient's recovery and willingness to follow treatment plans. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h9)
